A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DELTA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and matchable, including v2's added Appendices E–F.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation experiments, memory-component ablations, pronoun and summarization evaluations, and GPU-memory measurements in Sections 5–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds context-dependent translation, Lithuanian–English evaluation, and further component and memory-window experiments.

M1.justification: The four memory components, sentence-wise retrieval/translation/update procedure, Algorithm 1 and component prompt templates are retained. Alternative memory windows are evaluated as supplementary experiments; the proposed DELTA procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained IWSLT2017, Guofeng and QMSum evaluations, v2 adds CTX-PRO's English–German mini.gender.opensubtitles context-dependent translation task and Lithuanian–English Europarl evaluation. These substantially extend discourse-specific testing, language coverage and represented domains.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain. Appendix E additionally compares DELTA against Context augmented with Proper Noun Records, explicitly reported as Model 7 in Table 10. This is a limited comparator addition.

E3.justification: Supplementary protocols use the first 1,000 CTX-PRO instances with generative accuracy, one randomly sampled 556-sentence Europarl document, and short-/long-term window sweeps including a growing window. Original benchmark settings and default memory sizes remain unchanged. Table 10's inconsistent parent-row references do not establish changes to the original ablation configurations.

E4.justification: Appendix E substantially extends v1's cumulative ablation with isolated component tests, a Context-plus-records control, and fixed/growing memory-window sensitivity analyses. Section 6 also adds a targeted context-dependent translation evaluation. The original distance, pronoun, summarization and memory-cost analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports t-test p-values below 0.05 for DELTA versus Sentence/Context on translation quality in En↔Xx and consistency in En↔Zh. The test design is unspecified, and no repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals are added; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports CTX-PRO accuracy of 51.0% for DELTA versus 29.7% for Sentence. Table 12 reports Lithuanian–English sCOMET of 87.96 versus 87.33/87.87 for Sentence/Context; Tables 10–11 add component/window results. Original tabulated scores are retained. v2 also removes v1's erroneous 2.22-point ablation gain; Table 4 implies 1.34 points.

T1.justification: The LTCR-1 and fuzzy-match definitions in Equations 1–2 and the memory-update mathematics retain their meaning. The explicit long-term-memory set expression is condensed into equivalent prose and the retained algorithm. No new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion extend the pronoun-accuracy claim to context-dependent translation, with the conclusion explicitly mentioning discourse-structure modeling. The central multi-level-memory contribution, headline translation improvements, omission avoidance and memory-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds interpretations of component complementarity and why bilingual summaries may make larger or growing windows unnecessary. Appendix F identifies spaCy coverage as a constraint on language selection. Section 5.2 removes the earlier Qwen2-7B/Doc2Doc qualification despite retaining the underlying scores; runtime limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a Europarl data-access link and the growing-window rule of one additional sentence pair per eight translated sentences. It removes the explicit Sentence-baseline prompt and Figure 2's backbone-model identification. Core hyperparameters, component prompts, hardware information and the code/data release link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to SelectIT, LCS and Wicks and Post's context-dependent evaluation work. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Updates to ReadAgent, multi-agent debate and translation-with-comparison references identify the same previously cited works and are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 condenses method, baseline, summarization and memory-cost prose, revises the abstract/conclusion and pronoun-analysis heading, and adds acknowledgments and Appendices E–F. The overall narrative and main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 10–12, with Table 10 partly redisplaying the retained Table 4 ablation. It adds DELTA-row shading in detailed benchmark tables and locally adjusts captions, sizing and placement. Existing figures and original result displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The targeted context-dependent test and independent-component/window analyses strengthen the empirical assessment of discourse handling and memory design beyond v1. The gain is limited by underspecified significance testing, the single-document low-resource evaluation, and inconsistent parent-row references in Table 10. These additions improve the evidence without resolving all reporting weaknesses.
